title: Trust Atom (Trust Graph v1)
description: One statement of trust: source trusts target, about content, to the degree value. This schema describes atoms as Trust Graph writes them (canonical form). Implementations may also accept numbers for value and other RFC 3339 offsets for timestamp on input, then write the canonical form. See https://github.com/trustgraph/trustgraph-rust-cli/blob/master/doc/protocol.md

source.description: Who makes the statement: an absolute URI, usually a DID. Must differ from target.

target.description: What the statement is about: an absolute URI (a DID, URL, urn:, or ipfs://<ID>).

content.description: What the trust is about: a topic, comma-separated tags, or a URI.

timestamp.description: When the statement was made (UTC). Required once signed; for one source, target and content, the latest wins.

value.description: How much the source trusts the target: a canonical xsd:decimal string in -1..=1 (-1 distrust, 0 neutral, 1 full trust), with at most 9 decimal places, no exponent, no '+', no trailing zeros, and 0 for zero.

replaces.description: The credential this one supersedes: ipfs:// and its credential ID (a CIDv1, raw codec, SHA2-256, base32).

extra.description: Application-specific fields: non-empty keys, string values. Opaque to JSON-LD (@json).
